structured_output.what_is_happening: A ~14-month-old Believe-launchpad token for Orgo (orgo.ai — "fast desktop infrastructure for AI agents", sub-second boot, computer-use agent SDK) went vertical: +296% on the hour on ~$166k of volume, with essentially ALL 6h volume concentrated in that single hour (vol_accel h1/h6 = 6.0, m5/h6 = 9.6). 238 unique buyers vs 150 unique sellers in the hour; 640 buys / 359 sells. The move has already cracked at the moment of capture: −45.9% on the GeckoTerminal 15m, −24% on the DexScreener 5m, i.e. roughly half the spike retraced within minutes. The most informative clue to the cause is in the same-ticker list: three zero-liquidity ORGO copycats were minted today (unix ~1790103522, i.e. within minutes of each other), one of them named "ycomb gives them 500k btw" — copycat naming strongly implies a Y Combinator acceptance/funding headline about Orgo is the catalyst. Context: price is ~0.00049 vs an ATH of 0.01745, so the token is ~97% below its 2025 high with 12.5k holders (RugCheck) accumulated on the way down. Structure is clean (mint/freeze renounced, LP burn 1.0, top-10 ex-locker 13.3%, zero insider/rat-trader flags, no paid boosts, 0 degen calls, 0 smart-money signals), and GMGN flags community_takeover = true. Liquidity is $62.7k against a $246k mcap and $166k of hourly volume — the pool was churned ~2.6x in an hour.

narrative.description: Orgo is a real AI-infrastructure startup (computer-use agents / instant cloud desktops, docs site, SDK) whose Believe-launched token is being repriced on what appears to be a fresh funding or Y Combinator headline. The story is 'real revenue-generating AI-agent startup with a token, priced at a $246k market cap, just got institutional validation' — it sits inside the durable 2026 AI-agent/computer-use narrative and inside the narrower Believe 'ICM / internet capital markets' narrative where startup news is supposed to repricelinked tokens.
narrative.why_spreading: Two ingredients that genuinely travel on crypto social: (1) a legible, checkable external catalyst (a named accelerator/funding event) attached to (2) a token trading ~97% below its high at a sub-$250k cap, which makes the 'asymmetric re-rate' pitch easy to post. The copycat mints within the same hour confirm attention arrived and that opportunists saw it. But the mechanics say the first wave is already done: all volume in one hour, a −46% 15m candle, only 238 unique buyers, and 14 GMGN page visits — that is a small crowd, not a broad discovery wave. The narrative may still be spreading on X while the price impulse is already unwinding.

token_connection.why_this_token: This is unambiguously the canonical Orgo asset: DexScreener profile present, official website orgo.ai plus docs.orgo.ai, official X (x.com/orgo), Telegram and Discord all attached to this contract; launched on Believe in July 2025 as the project's own token; mint/freeze renounced and LP burned. If the catalyst is a real Orgo corporate headline, this is the instrument that expresses it. The caveat is category, not identity: a Believe token is a social/fee-share token, not equity — there is no contractual mechanism by which a YC cheque accrues to holders, so the link is narrative rather than economic.

authenticity.evidence: Pro-organic: no DexScreener paid ad, no paid boost, no paid trending bar; degen_call_count = 0 and smart_money_signal_count = 0 (no call-channel or tracker amplification detected); fresh_wallet_rate only 2.1%; bot_degen_rate 11.2%; top_rat_trader_pct 0.0; dev/creator hold rate 0.0; top70 sniper hold rate 0.0; zero insiders flagged in top holders and zero insider networks; creator is the Believe program address (57,297 tokens launched) rather than a serial ruggger; project X rename history is short and benign (orgohq -> orgo). 238 distinct buyers and 150 distinct sellers in an hour is a real, if small, crowd rather than a handful of wallets wash-trading. Against: the fresh_wallets = 1000 and bundler_wallets = 1000 figures look like API caps rather than true counts, so I cannot verify the bundler share; top_entrapment_trader_pct is 9.85%, non-trivial; the entire move is one hour of volume equal to 2.6x the pool, with a −46% 15m retrace, which is the profile of a fast reflexive spike into thin depth where early buyers distributed into the momentum; and GMGN's community_takeover = true plus only 14 page visits suggests a small coordinating group rather than broad organic discovery.

Telegram and Discord content is invisible. I also cannot see whether the buying was concentrated in a few large tickets behind the 238 addresses.

structural_risks: Massive overhead supply: price is ~97% below the 0.01745 ATH with 12,557 holders accumulated on the way down — every rally hands exit liquidity to underwater 2025 bagholders, which is the single strongest mechanical argument for fade.

Thin absolute depth: $62.7k pool liquidity ($77.9k total market liquidity) just absorbed $166k of hourly volume, ~2.6x turnover. Slippage is punishing; a single $10-20k exit moves price double digits.
50% of supply sits in a Jupiter Locker with an unknown unlock/vesting schedule (FDV $492k vs mcap $246k). An unlock or vested-team distribution is an unquantifiable supply overhang.
Mutable metadata flagged by RugCheck (owner can change token metadata).
Single pool, single DEX (Meteora), discovered_pairs = 1 — no depth redundancy and no CEX bid to absorb profit-taking.

Holder-distribution disagreement: RugCheck reports 12,557 holders with top-10 at 13.3% ex-locker, while GeckoTerminal reports 2,645 holders with top-10 at 73.7% (likely including the locker/pool). The true float concentration is not cleanly resolvable from the packet.
Velocity risk: the -24% 5m / -46% 15m retrace already occurred before the decision point, meaning the report is being written into an unwinding move rather than a building one.
No economic claim on the underlying company — a Believe token gives holders no equity or cash-flow right to any funding event, so the re-rate is pure narrative and reverts when attention leaves.

structured_output.counterargument: The strongest case against my fade call: this is not a memecoin with a fabricated story — it is a genuine operating AI-infrastructure company with a product, docs and SDK, and the catalyst appears to be a verifiable external event (YC/$500k funding) rather than a chart. News-driven repricings of real-company tokens behave differently from memecoin pumps: the first hour is bots and alert-followers, the first −40% candle shakes them out, and then the actual audience — people who read the announcement hours later, AI-agent-narrative traders, Believe/ICM communities — arrives across the following 6-24 hours and marks a higher low. At a $246k market cap for a YC-backed computer-use-agent company, the 'this is mispriced' pitch is unusually easy to spread, and comparable Believe tokens have run multi-day on much weaker news. Supporting details: promotion flags are all clean (no paid ads, no boosts, no call channels), so nothing here looks manufactured; the token is still 97% below ATH so there is enormous room before technical resistance from the 2025 distribution zone actually binds; LP is 100% burned and the dev holds 0%, so the classic dump vectors are closed; and the appearance of three copycats within minutes is evidence that attention is arriving, not leaving. If the official @orgo account amplifies the news during US evening hours, a $63k pool re-rates violently on very little fresh capital, and my 'peaking' call would look like I confused normal post-spike digestion with exhaustion.

structured_output.thesis: A real AI-agent infrastructure company's Believe token is being repriced on an apparent YC/funding headline — a legitimate, legible catalyst inside a live 2026 narrative, on a structurally clean token (LP burned, authorities renounced, dev holds zero, no paid promotion, no insider flags). But the trade is already mechanically exhausted at the decision point: 100% of the 6h volume landed in one hour, the pool turned over 2.6x against only $63k of depth, and price has already given back roughly half the move (−46% on the 15m) before this report is frozen. Crucially, the token sits ~97% below its ATH with over 12,000 holders accumulated on the descent plus 50% of supply in a locker — an overhead supply wall that converts every subsequent bid into exit liquidity. Only 238 unique buyers and 14 GMGN page visits indicate the crowd that showed up was small, and with zero call-channel or smart-money amplification there is no obvious second wave queued. My expectation over the next 6 hours is decaying volume, a lower-high structure and price settling well below the spike top, while the narrative itself keeps a residual bid and prevents a full round-trip to the pre-news $60-80k cap. I am calling fade rather than strong fade precisely because the catalyst is externally real: unlike a pure memecoin, a genuine funding headline can pull in a delayed, slower audience, so a higher low above pre-news levels is the likelier floor than a complete collapse.
